title: Cheaper process: shift or slide?

predict.q: A new process cuts the cost of producing every unit by 20%. What happens on the firm's long-run average cost diagram?

options.s: The whole LRAC curve shifts down: lower cost at every output
options.fb: Every point falls by 20%: the lowest point moves from 10 to 8, still at 1,000 units.

options.s: The firm moves down along its existing LRAC to a larger output
options.fb: That is an economy of scale: a movement along the same curve as output grows. A cheaper process lowers cost at every output, so the curve itself shifts.

options.s: Nothing on the diagram changes; only the price falls
options.fb: Costs fall, so the cost curve must move; the price is a separate decision.

options.s: The LRAC curve shifts up, because the new machines are expensive
options.fb: The machines are a one-off investment; the cost of producing each unit falls, so LRAC shifts down.

task: Move the cost saving slider from 0% to 20% and watch the LRAC curve and its lowest point. Then switch on "Grow output".

target.do: Move the cost saving slider to 20%, then press Check.

takeaway: Technology shifts the curve; growing bigger moves you along it.
explore: "Grow output" slides the dot along LRAC1 from 500 to 1,000 units: an economy of scale, a movement along the curve.
